title: The equivalence of finite-path perfect matching and \(\mathsf{ATR}_0\)
statement:
Let $athsf{PM}$ denote the perfect matching principle, and let $ext{Finite Path }\mathsf{PM}$ denote its restriction to finite-path instances. Let $peratorname{\mathsf{ATR}}_0$ and $peratorname{\mathsf{RCA}}_0$ be the indicated systems of reverse mathematics.

**Finite-path perfect matching conjecture.** $ext{Finite Path }\mathsf{PM}$ is equivalent to $peratorname{\mathsf{ATR}}_0$ over $peratorname{\mathsf{RCA}}_0$.

The paper proves that finite-path perfect matching is close in strength to $peratorname{\mathsf{ATR}}_0$ and asks whether it implies that system, as well as whether $peratorname{\mathsf{ATR}}_0$ proves finite-path perfect matching or perfect matching. The supplied text does not resolve these questions.
source_name: Stephen Flood, Matthew Jura, Oscar Levin and Tyler Markkanen, “The computational strength of matchings in countable graphs”, arXiv:2006.11334 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.11334

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2020).
